elaine: Quick UX question — we need a final decision on revoke timing + confirm dialog for API keys. Figma has three patterns: hard delete immediately, soft revoke (suspend + auto-delete after 7d), and soft revoke with explicit user 'delete' step. Which do we ship for GA? mike: leaning soft revoke with 7d auto-delete + undo toast. Gives devs a safety net and matches other product flows. jess: +1 on soft revoke. But we need to nail the confirm modal copy and CTA order so users don’t accidentally escalate. Also a11y: screenreader announce and focus management. elaine: exactly — two main questions: copy + CTA ordering, and accessibility behavior. Proposed copy options below. Thoughts? mike: love options. For CTA order I prefer Primary = "Revoke" (danger style), Secondary = "Cancel". But thinking about humans, we might want the safer action as primary? tamir: accessibility-wise primary should be the destructive action visually prominent, but focus should land on the cancel/neutral button to avoid accidental keyboard activation. Screenreader should announce the consequences. jess: agree with tamir. Pattern: visually emphasize Delete/Revoke, but put focus on "Cancel" when modal opens. Also include a clear 1-line summary of impact. elaine: proposed copy A/B: (1) short + direct, (2) more explanatory. elaine: Copy A - short "Revoke API key? This key will stop working immediately. You can restore it within 7 days from the Keys page." elaine: Copy B - explanatory "Revoke API key Revoking will suspend this key immediately. Calls using this key will fail. The key will be permanently deleted after 7 days. During that window you can restore it from Settings → API keys." mike: prefer B for clarity for non-technical folks. Less risk of support tickets. tamir: minor nit: include exact restore location path (Settings → API keys). Good call. jess: +1 to adding location. Also we should display last-used timestamp and scopes in the modal so the user can confirm they’re revoking the right key. elaine: good call. UX checklist for modal: header, 1-line consequence, last-used + scopes, undo window, primary/secondary buttons, accessibility hooks. design-bot: Accessibility notes: recommend role="alertdialog", aria-labelledby referencing header, aria-describedby referencing the consequence paragraph; set focus entry on cancel button. Provide aria-live="polite" for the undo toast. tamir: sample snippet for dialog behavior (for eng): ```html

Revoke API key

Revoking will suspend this key immediately. It will be permanently deleted after 7 days. Restore from Settings → API keys.

``` mike: UX for toast: show "Key revoked — Undo" toast pinned top-right for 7s. Undo restores the key and logs an audit event. After 7 days background job purges key. jess: timeline text on modal: "Will be permanently deleted: 7 days from now (MM/DD)" showing exact date reduces confusion. elaine: what about copy for undo toast and audit message? Proposals: - Toast: "API key revoked — Undo" (button: "Undo") - Audit log entry: "Key revoked by — pending deletion in 7 days" tamir: also consider an option for admins to change grace period org-wide. Might not ship now, but add to backend design notes. mike: keyboard pattern: Enter must not trigger destructive action when modal opens. Esc closes modal (same as Cancel). That supports focus-on-cancel pattern. jess: accessibility nit: when undo toast appears, avoid stealing focus. Use aria-live polite so SR reads it but keyboard focus stays where user expects. elaine: final decision proposal (for this sprint): - Default: soft revoke with 7-day auto-delete - Modal: Copy B (expanded), include last-used + scopes + deletion date - Visual: Primary = Revoke (danger), Secondary = Cancel; initial focus set to Cancel - Toast: "API key revoked — Undo" with aria-live polite and 7s timer - Keyboard: Esc == Cancel, Enter on focused Cancel triggers cancel; Enter on focused Revoke triggers revoke mike: ship it. I'll sync with eng on focus behavior and toast implementation. tamir: I'll add aria props + code snippet to the PR. Also logging/audit text will be in the API. jess: I'll update the Figma modal with copy B + the last-used row and the exact deletion date field. elaine: thanks team — can someone add this as an action item on the keyflow ticket? @mike? mike: done — added to FLOW-238 in Jira. :white_check_mark: design-bot: Deploy bot: note — staging build with modal copy changes will run preview on /staging in ~20m. elaine: perfect, closing this thread. If any follow-ups ping me. :slightly_smiling_face:
